OPL No: OPL-GA-1201A-01
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL)
CALIBER purposes only   Sheet 1 of 1
OPL Title   Mechanical Seal Flush (API Plan 11) Verification   Discipline   Mechanical
Equipment   GA-1201A - HEXANE FEED PUMP   Area / Unit   1200 - HEXANE FEED SYSTEM
Related Interlock SEQ-1201 (SIL 1)   P&ID; Ref   TJC-LLD-PID-1201
Classification: [ ] Basic Knowledge   [ ] Improvement   [X] Trouble Case   Aspect: P-Q-C-D-S-M-E
1. PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE
This One Point Lesson explains mechanical seal flush (api plan 11) verification for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP) in
the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM. Confirm seal flush dP > 1.5 bar before start. Low flush = seal face overheating and hexane
leak to atmosphere. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so
the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
2. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Hazard note: this equipment is HIGH CRITICAL handling n-Hexane at up to 16 barg / 80 degC. Observe the following before
and during the task:
n Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
n Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
n Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
n Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
n Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.
3. TOOLS & MATERIALS REQUIRED
l Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
l LOTO padlocks and permit
l Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
l Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
l Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
l Lifting gear and slings (certified)
4. DETAILED PROCEDURE / STEPS
Step   Action   Check / Acceptance
1   Line up discharge flush to seal chamber and open flush isolation   Isolation & LOTO verified
2   Check PDI-1201 reads 1.5-2.5 bar dP across the flush orifice RO-1201   Parts match BOM / spec
3   Verify no visible leak or drip at the gland / seal drain   Torque / clearance to spec
4   If dP low, isolate and inspect orifice RO-1201 for plugging by polymer/dirt   No leak / smooth operation
5   Confirm quench (Plan 62) N2/steam is lined up to the outboard side   Record in equipment history
5. COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING
Symptom   Likely Cause   Action
Hexane leak observed at GA-1201A   API Plan 11 flush orifice RO-1201 partially   Replaced JC T2100 mechanical seal cartridge,
seal gland during operation, seal dr.   plugged causing seal face.   cleaned flush orifice, v.
GA-1201A tripped on VSHH-1201 high   Angular misalignment 0.12 mm/100mm after   Laser re-aligned pump/motor, re-shimmed
vibration 7.4 mm/s   foundation settlement   motor feet, vibration back to.
Bearing DE noisy with rising   Outer race spalling on DE bearing due to   Renewed DE bearing 7310 BECBM, flushed
temperature TI-1201 trend   prolonged misalignment   housing, refilled ISO VG 68
6. KEY LEARNING POINTS
n Confirm seal flush dP > 1.5 bar before start. Low flush = seal face overheating and hexane leak to atmosphere.
n Respect the interlock SEQ-1201: e.g. PSLL-1201 trips at < 0.5 barg - never defeat it without a permit.
n Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID; TJC-LLD-PID-1201 before working on GA-1201A.
n Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.

1. PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE
This One Point Lesson explains tube-side cleaning (hydrojetting) for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT
HEATING SYSTEM. Hexane fouling on the tube side raises the differential pressure (PDT-5605) and cuts the heat duty,
leaving cold solvent downstream. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step
method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
2. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Hazard note: this equipment is LOW CRITICAL handling Hexane / MP Steam at up to 16 barg (tube) / 200 degC. Observe
the following before and during the task:
n Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
n Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
n Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
n Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
n Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.
3. TOOLS & MATERIALS REQUIRED
l Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
l LOTO padlocks and permit
l Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
l Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
l Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
l Lifting gear and slings (certified)
4. DETAILED PROCEDURE / STEPS
Step   Action   Check / Acceptance
1   Isolate and drain both sides, then purge with nitrogen   Isolation & LOTO verified
2   Open the channel cover and remove the old gasket   Parts match BOM / spec
3   Hydrojet the tube bores and inspect for pitting/erosion   Torque / clearance to spec
4   Verify tube-side dP restored and no residual blockage   No leak / smooth operation
5   Re-gasket with new SW SS316 gasket and box up to torque   Record in equipment history
5. COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING

damaged   pattern

steam use   condensate temperature

1. PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE
This One Point Lesson explains psv-5607 testing & car-seal management for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the
SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. The tube-side relief valve is the exchanger's overpressure protection and must be proven
and never isolated in service. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step
method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.
2. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Hazard note: this equipment is LOW CRITICAL handling Hexane / MP Steam at up to 16 barg (tube) / 200 degC. Observe
the following before and during the task:
n Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
n Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
n Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
n Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
n Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.
3. TOOLS & MATERIALS REQUIRED
l Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
l LOTO padlocks and permit
l Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
l Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
l Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
l Lifting gear and slings (certified)
4. DETAILED PROCEDURE / STEPS
Step   Action   Check / Acceptance
1   Confirm PSV-5607 is set to 16 barg on the nameplate   Isolation & LOTO verified
2   Carry out an off-line pop test per the statutory schedule   Parts match BOM / spec
3   Keep the PSV inlet/outlet isolation car-sealed open in service   Torque / clearance to spec
4   Record the test certificate and next due date   No leak / smooth operation
5   Never block-in a live PSV without an authorised spare   Record in equipment history
5. COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING
Symptom   Likely Cause   Action
High tube dP PDT-5605, low solvent   Hexane fouling / polymer fines deposit on tube   Hydrojetted 246 tubes, restored dP and duty,
outlet temperature   bores   re-gasketed
Hexane weep at channel flange   Spiral-wound channel gasket relaxed /   Renewed channel gasket, re-torqued in cross
damaged   pattern
Continuous steam at condensate, high   Steam trap element failed open   Replaced steam trap element, verified
steam use   condensate temperature
6. KEY LEARNING POINTS
